content.text:
I checked the brief line by line against the 8-K Exhibit 99.1.

**Notable findings:**
- The **$563 million severance special item** — the largest of the quarter's special items — never appears in the brief, even though the brief's watch item does pick up the $237 million MDL provision. That makes the special-items fact only half-conveyed.
- The **balance sheet comparison is mislabeled**: the release compares June 30, 2026 to **September 30, 2025** (prior fiscal year end), not to a "prior year period" quarter. Both the total assets and total liabilities claims inherit that error.
- The $4.8 billion GAAP opex dollar figure is omitted (the 19% growth and personnel driver are correct), and the brief never notes that opex growth outpaced the 14% revenue growth, nor that international transaction revenue was the slowest-growing category — both are characterizations rather than misstatements.

facts.evidence: Net revenue totaled $11.6 billion for the quarter, reflecting a 14% year-over-year increase or 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP earnings per share were $2.97, up 10%
non-GAAP earnings per share stood at $3.32, marking an 11% rise
Data processing revenue increased 17% to $6.0 billion
GAAP operating expenses rose 19% primarily driven by personnel expenses. (The $4.8 billion level and the comparison to 14% revenue growth are omitted, but nothing stated is wrong.)

Payments volume increased 10% year-over-year on a constant-dollar basis for the three months ended June 30, 2026 ... Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe transactions grew 12% on a constant-dollar basis
The company executed share repurchases and dividends totaling $6.2 billion during the period.
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities stood at $13.9 billion as of June 30, 2026.

Monitor the trajectory of litigation provisions, which included a $237 million charge for the interchange multidistrict litigation case and a $253 million provision in the current quarter's operating expenses. (The $237M MDL item is correct, but the $563 million severance special item is nowhere in the brief, so the quarter's special items are conveyed incompletely.)
international transaction revenue grew 6% to $3.9 billion

claims.claim: Visa reported GAAP net income of $5.6 billion, a 7% increase over the prior year.
Non-GAAP net income reached $6.3 billion, an 8% increase.
Net revenue totaled $11.6 billion for the quarter, a 14% year-over-year increase.
Net revenue increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP earnings per share were $2.97, up 10%.
Non-GAAP earnings per share were $3.32, up 11%.
Share repurchases and dividends totaled $6.2 billion during the period.
Payments volume increased 10% year-over-year on a constant-dollar basis for the three months ended June 30, 2026.
Processed transactions rose 10% year-over-year.
Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe transactions grew 12% on a constant-dollar basis.
Total cross-border volume expanded 13%.
Data processing revenue increased 17% to $6.0 billion.
International transaction revenue grew 6% to $3.9 billion.
Other revenue surged 45% to $1.5 billion.
Client incentives amounted to $4.7 billion, an 18% increase over the prior year.
GAAP operating expenses rose 19%, primarily driven by personnel expenses.
Management stated that consumer and business spending remains resilient, with the strategy continuing to deliver strong performance across consumer payments, commercial, and money movement solutions.
The company is designing, building, and shipping products at an increased velocity to position Visa, its clients, and the ecosystem to capture future opportunities.
No specific numerical guidance or outlook figures were provided in this release regarding future quarters or full-year targets.
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities stood at $13.9 billion as of June 30, 2026.
The company had $28.4 billion of remaining authorized funds for share repurchases as of the quarter end.
Total assets decreased to $94.59 billion from $99.627 billion in the prior year period.
claims.note: Figures match the balance sheet, but the comparison period is mislabeled: $99,627 million is the September 30, 2025 fiscal year-end balance, not a prior-year comparable period (June 30, 2025 is not presented).

claims.claim: Total liabilities declined to $59.412 billion from $61.718 billion in the prior year period.
claims.note: Same period error: $61,718 million is the September 30, 2025 fiscal year-end figure, not a prior-year period balance.

claims.claim: Litigation provisions included a $237 million charge for the interchange multidistrict litigation case.
The current quarter's operating expenses included a $253 million litigation provision.
GAAP earnings per share growth was approximately 9% on a constant-dollar basis, excluding foreign currency impacts.
Client incentives rose 18% to $4.7 billion.
Client incentives significantly influence the net revenue calculation.
